Some useful functional groups were well tolerated. Substituents including both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups at the para position were investigated. Benzoic acid (2a) was obtained in 57% yield from benzyl alcohol (1a) under the standard conditions together with a 38% NMR yield of the intermediate benzaldehyde product (Table 1, entry 1). When the loading of TEMPO was increased to 30 mol%, the yield of benzoic acid increased to 73% along with a 14% NMR yield of benzaldehyde (entry 2). results.question: What aryl group (Ar) is used for compound 1a in the paper (how is Ar defined for 1a)?
results.system_answer: Retrieved molecule identity evidence: Hydroxyl groups are a class of common, versatile, and reactive functional groups in organic chemistry. In organic synthesis, the hydroxyl groups are usually protected when a targeted reaction is to be carried out selectively with another functionality. p-Methoxybenzyl (PMB) ethers are among the most frequently used protecting groups in organic synthesis.[1] In multi-step synthesis, the alcohols would be protected as PMB ethers, which were deprotected usually with DDQ (2,3-dichloro-5,6- dicyano-1,4-benzoquinone),[2a–k] Li/NH3, [2l] or TFA (trifluoroacetic acid)[2m] first to release the hydroxyl group. Subsequent oxidation with stoichiometric amounts of oxidants such as TPAP/NMO (tetrapropylammonium perruthenate/N-methylmorpholine oxide),[2a] PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate),[2b,c] dimethyl sulfoxide,[2d,e] DMP (Dess-Martin periodinane),[2f–l] BAIB ((diacetoxyiodo)benzene),[2k] and IBX (2-iodylbenzoic acid)[2m] would afford aldehydes or ketones (Scheme 1a). Such synthetic operation lacks the step economy and is environmentally unfriendly. Molecular oxygen, an important component of air, is eco-friendly and inexpensive. Thus, catalytic aerobic oxidation of PMB ethers to carbonyl compounds would be an ideal solution.
